predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's 540 shape of Glywysing, cut out of the sub-Roman Brythonic lands: south Wales between the Neath and the Rhymney

successors.name: Norman England
successors.text: the lowlands of Glamorgan (the Vale), parcelled out to Robert Fitzhamon's followers as the Lordship of Glamorgan

ledger.x: 942: Morgan Hen unites Gwent and Glywysing as Morgannwg.
975: Gwent is separate from Morgannwg again.

c. 1090: Robert Fitzhamon deposes Iestyn ap Gwrgant and the Normans take Glamorgan. The Iestyn page: he was 'deposed c. 1090 by Norman ruler Robert Fitzhamon', the lowlands were parcelled out to Fitzhamon's followers and the mountains left in Welsh control (the lords of Afan); the Morgannwg page has the conquest…

wars.name: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's conquest of Wales
wars.outcome: Gruffydd conquered Gwent and Glywysing in about 1055 and held them until his death in 1063, when the native line under Caradog ap Gruffudd regained Glywysing.

wars.name: Norman invasion of south-east Wales
wars.outcome: The Normans reached Striguil by 1071 and Caerleon by 1086, extinguishing the Kingdom of Gwent; the attacks faltered after Roger de Breteuil forfeited his estates in 1075.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Glamorgan
wars.outcome: Robert Fitzhamon deposed Iestyn ap Gwrgant c.

certainty.note: The pages say the borders of Glywysing were uncertain and changed over time; no treaty or survey line is given.
